access_detail: HF MedOtter/BUS-UCLM (public, ungated, CC-BY-4.0): one parquet (319 MB, 683 rows, 856x606 screenshots + mask column). datasets-server /info, /first-rows and /statistics work; fetch_hf streams it and skips the `mask` column by name.

submodality.resolvable_by: registry hard b-mode ultrasound is right for about 94% (646 of 683, has_doppler=False); the 37 has_doppler=True rows (5.4%) and 6 has_combined rows carry a colour-Doppler overlay. Boolean columns are not mapped by metalabel, so nothing overrides the hard label.

domain.resolvable_by: registry multi oncology (normal class is 61% of rows, so oncology is a screening domain, fine)

problems: 5% of rows are Doppler/combined screens but labelled hard b-mode (low impact; no per-row way to exclude them in the HF-streaming route).
ClassLabel-like column `class_label` (benign/malignant/normal) is a diagnosis and correctly unmapped.
Same split group `busi` as BUSI although it is a different cohort (Univ. Castilla-La Mancha); fine for leakage, no duplicate pixels expected.
notes: Clean dataset-level labels; all 683 images are breast ultrasound. 419 are 'normal' (no lesion) images.

access_detail: Zenodo 15702341 (open): single OralTriD.zip, 2.81 GB, below the 20 GB budget so it is downloaded whole. Central directory read: 808 jpg in OLP/OLK/OBU `Images/` folders (high-resolution phone/camera photos), 808 LabelMe json in `Annotations/`, train_val_split.csv.

columns_or_levels: d2=disease code (OLP lichen planus, OLK leukoplakia, OBU benign ulcer)

domain.resolvable_by: registry masked; the three diseases (oral lichen planus, leukoplakia, benign ulcer) have no obvious class (dermatology / otolaryngology both defensible), keep masked

problems: Annotations json are matched by is_mask (folder `Annotations`) so only the 808 jpgs become images.
Disease codes OLP/OLK/OBU/OBC map to nothing in match_value (verified), which is correct: they are diagnoses.
No MMBU-public clinical photograph shows an oral cavity (public clinical photography = 31 images, body_part masked, domain surgery), so body_part oral cavity rests on the dataset description only.
notes: Everything dataset-level and correct. 808 images vs plan 808.

access_detail: figshare 22302559 (open, CC0): one NeoJaundice.zip, 440 MB, downloaded whole. Read via a ranged zip central directory: 2,235 jpg (NeoJaundice/images/<patient>-<1|2|3>.jpg) + one metadata csv. (figshare ndownloader needs a fresh signed redirect per range request; remotezip's HEAD fails with 403, the sampler never needs it because the zip is under budget.)

columns_or_levels: file suffix -1/-2/-3 = which of three skin sites (order not documented in the record)

body_part.resolvable_by: registry candidates [face, skin] is incomplete: the paper (web) says three skin photos per infant of head, face and chest. Fix to candidates [chest, face, head, skin]; the suffix -1/-2/-3 would resolve it per sample but the mapping is not stated in the record.

domain.resolvable_by: registry multi hepatology (neonatal jaundice); no pediatrics class

problems: body_part candidates miss `chest` and `head`: the dataset has chest photos and the registry set [face, skin] would give them a wrong-only candidate set (skin still covers them, so partial-label loss is not wrong, but face is).
Three photos per infant are near-duplicate framing of one patient (745 patients, 2,235 images); spread_sample spreads by parent folder (all in one folder), so a random 2,000 of 2,235 is fine.
Registry says plan 2,000 of 2,235 effective; OK.
notes: Tabular metadata is clinical (bilirubin, weight) and maps to nothing; the label fix is dataset-level.

access_detail: HF sada-group/CryoLithe-training-dataset (public, MIT): 1,536 files, 936 GB, all `.mrc` volumes (1,017; up to 2 GB each) and `.tlt`/`.rawtlt` tilt-angle text files (369). No datasets-server config (no builder), so fetch_hf falls to the file listing: kind('.mrc') is 'other', no media, no archives -> state error 'no media files or archives listed'. prepare.find_media also has no reader for .mrc (mrcfile is not in requirements.txt).

columns_or_levels: file suffix = raw tilt series / cryo-CARE+IsoNet recon / Icecream recon

submodality.resolvable_by: registry hard cryo-electron tomography (tilt series + denoised reconstructions of EMPIAR-11830/11058)

body_part.resolvable_by: registry hard cells (EMPIAR-11830 are cryo-FIB lamellae of mixed cell types)

problems: Nothing downloadable or readable as selected: .mrc is not a known media kind in files.py and prepare.py has no MRC reader; the 936 GB repo would also blow any budget (hf budget is hard-coded 50 GiB in fetch_hf, not --max-gb).
Three other cryo-ET datasets are selected (cryoet-jove-dl-training-data, membrain-seg-training-data, ankyrin-g-axon-initial-segment-cryoet-2026), so the class is not lost.

If kept, needs: MRC added to VOLUME_EXT, mrcfile in requirements, and a header-plus-ranged-slice reader (MRC is raw slices after a 1,024-byte header, so HTTP Range can fetch single slices of a 2 GB file).
notes: Drop. It is also marked split=val, so dropping removes a validation set for cryo-ET; the other three cryo-ET sets are train.

access_detail: Zenodo 10688100 (open, CC-BY-4.0): `HER2 COHORTE 2 IMAGES.zip` (194 MB, downloaded whole) + `DATA HER2 TQI.xlsx` (20.8 MB, fetched as metadata, <50 MB). Central directory: 174 jpg = 87 `HER2NNN.jpg` at the top level + 87 same-named files in a `Nueva Carpeta/` subfolder (different byte sizes: a second image set, presumably the vimentin set given the 'VIMENTIN CUANTIF' sheets), plus Log.txt (ImageJ quantification) and a second copy of the xlsx.

metadata_sources.location: DATA HER2 TQI.xlsx (sheets: HCVB SAMPLE DATA, DIAGS BIN, VIMENTIN CUANTIF 1/2, CUANTIF V1/V2)

columns_or_levels: file, mean, count, area, size (no header)

stain.resolvable_by: registry candidates [ihc, vimentin] is right: both sets are IHC (HER2 and vimentin). Nothing in the file names separates them (folder 'Nueva Carpeta' is not a class), so it stays candidates.

problems: Only 174 images exist (plan 1,000, effective -1): the quota is not reachable, so about 826 planned slots are empty.

`DATA HER2 TQI.xlsx` has a 197 MB uncompressed sheet1.xml (20.8 MB zipped); openpyxl in non-read-only mode will use several GB of RAM and take minutes in metalabel. Use read_only=True or skip xlsx > 10 MB.
The xlsx contains diagnosis (HER2 score) columns: correctly unmapped.

Every top-level image has a same-named twin in Nueva Carpeta; `key_candidates` joins by file stem/name, so the table join by `HER2NNN.jpg` is ambiguous (two images per key) - harmless since no Pass-2 field comes from the table.
notes: Small but clean. Tile-level brightfield IHC of breast tissue.

access_detail: Zenodo 17913303 (open): single TIRF_SYNAPSE_LFA1_repo_v1.0.zip, 870 MB, downloaded whole and fully extracted. Central directory (3,296 members): raw_tirf_images/00_Raw_images = 352 tif (88 synapses x cd3, dic, lfa1, factin; one factin missing), plus about 2,300 DERIVED tif in analysis_output (background-subtracted copies, ROI crops, preprocessed, centred crops, radial spin stacks, mask tifs, Removed/) and macros / R scripts / csv / pzfx.

columns_or_levels: intensity profiles, no image-level Pass-2 field

modality.resolvable_by: registry hard fluorescence microscopy is wrong for the 88 `_dic.tif` raw images (DIC, transmitted light: light microscopy / contrast microscopy). Exclude them instead of relabelling (a hard label cannot be overridden by metadata).

submodality.resolvable_by: registry hard TIRF is right for cd3/lfa1/factin (raw TIRF); wrong for dic. `text_hits` on `_dic.tif` returns contrast microscopy + TIRF both strong.

stain.resolvable_by: registry masked. Channel token gives a per-sample stain: lfa1, cd3 = antibody -> immunofluorescence; factin -> phalloidin (probable, not stated in the record). Use candidates [immunofluorescence, phalloidin] at dataset level; file-token rule would resolve it.

specimen.resolvable_by: registry hard human (T cells; record does not say primary vs cell line)

problems: Without exclude_paths about 2,650 'images' pass is_mask/kind, of which only 352 are raw; >85% are derived crops, spins, mask-like tifs and background-subtracted copies of the same 88 synapses (duplicates in dHash terms are removed only if identical).
After exclude `(^|/)(analysis_output|imagej_macros|r_scripts)/|_dic\.tif$` 264 raw fluorescence images remain (88 cd3, 88 lfa1, 87 factin, 1 unnamed) vs plan 3,000.
Raw tif are ~2 MB each (single frame, 16-bit): read_image handles them.
notes: Keep with the exclude and the stain candidates; expect 264 images, not 3,000. All 88 synapses appear as 3 channels (near-duplicate cells).

access_detail: method doi -> https://doi.org/10.6019/S-BIAD3802 resolves to www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/studies/S-BIAD3802, which resolve_doi does not handle (raises Manual 'unsupported host'). The BioStudies JSON API does list files: GET /biostudies/api/v1/studies/S-BIAD3802/files?limit=100 returns 95 TIFF movies (hSyn_GCaMP6s 30, Slc17a7_IRES2_CrexAi162D 30, hSyn_RiboL1_jGCaMP8s 35), each 927 MB, 81.9 GB total, 5 axial resolutions x 19 FOV/depth combinations. The ftp mirror path guesses 404.

submodality.resolvable_by: registry hard multiphoton microscopy (two-photon time series)

stain.resolvable_by: registry masked (GCaMP is a genetically encoded indicator, not in the stain vocabulary)

problems: resolve_doi cannot handle BioStudies, so as selected the row ends in state manual.

Even with a BioStudies lister (there is a clean JSON API) every file is a 927 MB 2D+t TIFF: the 20 GB budget fits about 22 files, and prepare reads 4 frames per file, so about 90 images vs plan 1,000, at 20 GB of transfer. The 95 files are the same 19 fields of view imaged at 5 resolutions (near-duplicates).
Same BioStudies unsupported-host problem hits oi-dic-smlm-correlative-biad3889 (not in this todo).
notes: Soft drop (cost/benefit), with a note that a BioStudies lister is easy if wanted.

body_part.resolvable_by: registry candidates [abdomen, chest, esophagus]. DICOM BodyPartExamined = ESOPHAGUS for every series (collection-level tag even for chest/abdomen protocols), so the DICOM rule would hard-label all slices esophagus; protocols are thorax + abdomen CT. Keep candidates.

problems: Not downloadable as selected (Manual).

If a TCIA lister were added: 17 of 126 series are SCOUT/Topograma localizers (2-D projection images with Modality CT), and coronal/sagittal reformats (ABD SAG/COR) are in the same collection: exclude `SCOUT|Topograma|localizer` series or the 2-D scouts would become 'conventional ct' images.
10.2 GB for 20,593 slices; 2,000 planned is easily reachable.

access_detail: figshare 28931402 (open, CC-BY-4.0) is only the ADI (adipose) article: one ADI.7z of 6.25 GB (<20 GB: downloaded whole, then py7zr-extracted by prepare). Header read with py7zr over ranged requests: 72,006 png 224x224 tiles named `<slide>_<x>_<y>_ADI.png` from 499 slides (150 tiles each). The other 7 classes are 7 more figshare articles (LYM 28936250, DEB 28939016, MUC 28939100, MUS 28939115, NORM 28939151, STR 28939169, TUM 28939460, 7-9.6 GB each); the registry fallback_urls list six of them and miss STR and TUM.

columns_or_levels: file tokens: slide id, tile x/y, class

submodality.resolvable_by: registry hard whole slide imaging (224x224 tiles cut from 20x Aperio WSIs; consistent with how the other tile datasets are labelled)

body_part.resolvable_by: registry candidates [colon, rectum]; correct (colorectal cancer resections)

problems: As selected the sample is a single tissue class (adipose, mostly pale fat tissue): 2,000 tiles of one class from 72,006. Fine for the Pass-2 heads (none is tissue-class), but low diversity per GB (6.25 GB for one class).

`MUS` (smooth muscle) is another class folder / file token: rules.py matches bare `mus` as mouse (strong). If the MUS article is ever added, `MUS/..._MUS.png` gets specimen=mouse strong (conflict with registry hard human; verified with text_hits). Remove bare `mus` from the mouse rule.
7z is solid: prepare extracts all 72k png (about 6.7 GB) just to keep 2,000.
related nct-crc-he-100k / crc-val-he-7k are the same tissue classes (different cohort), in separate split groups: no leakage, visually similar.
notes: Keep; consider adding other class articles (needs multi-ref support in select_datasets/download).
